prompt: A single panoramic diagram shows a vast pretrained model as a swirling gray fog of text and code tokens, fed by rivers of books and repositories, outputting only fluent next-token predictions that remain an unfinished base. Sequential chambers then transform it: a supervised-fine-tuning workshop where the model copies curated example cards of instructions, reasoning traces and working software; a reinforcement-learning arena whose scoreboards, staffed by human graders and other models, award points for preferred answers while adding refusal shields; and a side hatch that injects supplemental engineering traces and company documents without restarting pretraining. A looping arrow from the finished model back to generating fresh training examples for the next version is labeled “not fully self-improving,” yet the modest, data-driven upgrade emerges on the far right as a sleek, product-ready assistant that follows instructions, reasons step by step, writes code and refuses certain requests, looking like an entirely different model.
